assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns protein degradation into a designable chemical event: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to remove targets rather than inhibit them. A new pharmacological modality, with a clear chemical mechanism and wide generality for biologists and drug hunters.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded and developed the PROTAC concept and its validation; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains the glue mechanism. Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray made important contributions, so the three-person limit forces a contestable cut.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the mechanism, and several degraders are in late clinical trials. Clinical approval of a PROTAC is still pending, which may argue for slightly more time.
uncertainties: Whether Crews, Deshaies and Handa is the fairest trio given Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray.
Clinical proof of benefit is incomplete.
Whether PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues should be one prize or are distinct discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that a mutant cysteine in KRAS G12C can be targeted covalently, which broke the long-held view that RAS is undruggable. The work rests on rigorous chemistry and chemical genetics of kinases, and it led to approved drugs for a major cancer driver.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean: Shokat's group made the decisive discovery of the switch-II pocket tethering strategy. Industrial teams developed the clinical compounds but built on his result. A single laureate is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adagrasib are approved and independently validated. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The chemical-genetic kinase work and the KRAS work are two parts; the committee must decide whether both are cited.
Resistance mechanisms are still emerging, though this does not undercut the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics made it possible to measure thousands of proteins and their modifications quantitatively. This is the analytical chemistry that turned cellular biochemistry into a measurable system, and I value quantitative measurement highly.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the leading figures of the field, covering high-accuracy MS-based proteomics, targeted and quantitative methods, and shotgun and multidimensional identification. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also strong, so credit is distributed and some exclusion is unavoidable.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature, widely reproduced and routinely used, so the field is ready for recognition. Some of the field's foundational ionization work was already honored in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for ionization may reduce the novelty of the claim.
Choosing three people from a large community is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs. It rewires translation chemistry and is now a general tool for protein engineering and for biological research.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pair and its use in living cells. Chin extended the approach to eukaryotes, to multiple codons and to quadruplet codons. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed, so credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: The technology is broadly reproduced for over two decades. Therapeutic and industrial applications are still developing, but the underlying discovery is mature.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Schultz versus Chin and Wang is open.
I am less sure about the exact priority relationships among the early orthogonal pair publications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, especially sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry with reversible terminators, transformed genomics and reduced the cost of sequencing by orders of magnitude. For genome stability and mutation research it is indispensable.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman developed the chemistry and single-molecule approach behind the Solexa/Illumina platform. Rothberg (pyrosequencing and 454), Ju and Mayer have competing claims, so the allocation of credit is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The impact is overwhelming and independently confirmed, with long clinical and research use. Timing is clearly appropriate.
uncertainties: Disputed priority between competing platforms.
Whether the prize is better suited to chemistry or to physiology or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base into another without double-strand breaks, by engineering deaminase chemistry on a Cas9 scaffold. This is a precise chemical solution with direct therapeutic relevance, and I would want to see how well it controls off-target and bystander editing.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and experimental development, with Komor and Gaudelli as first authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors. Nishida and Kondo made a parallel cytidine deaminase version. Liu also appears in B046 (prime editing), which could be combined.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs confirm the editors, and early clinical applications have appeared. Because CRISPR was already recognized in 2020, this is a follow-on that may be considered somewhat early.
uncertainties: Premature relative to long-term clinical safety data.
Whether the prize would be given to Liu alone for base and prime editing.
Parallel work by Nishida and Kondo.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation shows that RNA carries a regulated chemical layer: writers, erasers and readers control mRNA fate. It links RNA chemistry to development, cancer and metabolism, and is an epitranscriptomic counterpart to chromatin chemistry.
assessment.attribution: He proposed reversible RNA methylation and identified FTO as an m6A demethylase; Jaffrey and Rechavi mapped m6A transcriptome-wide. Others (Jia, Dominissini, Meyer, Yang) also contributed, so credit is spread out.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and growing, but I am concerned about the quantitation and antibody-based mapping, which has produced discrepancies between methods. Some claims about physiological function remain contested.
uncertainties: Method-dependent disagreement in m6A site mapping and stoichiometry.
The functional importance of FTO as an m6A eraser is debated.
Attribution among many contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles made it possible to deliver siRNA and mRNA in vivo, and enabled mRNA vaccines and RNAi therapeutics. It is a chemistry-driven delivery solution of very large medical consequence.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and Madden developed the core formulation and the ionizable lipid principle at UBC and in the associated companies. MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed lipid chemistry and delivery science, so the best trio is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Impact is proven by billions of vaccine doses and approved siRNA drugs. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized nucleoside modification, which may reduce appetite for a second mRNA-related prize soon.
uncertainties: Contested credit across several academic and industrial groups.
Possible overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize.
Patent and industrial history complicates attribution.
